title: GTA 6 and Duolingo had a baby.  Getting 10-15 signups a day on this.
author: Master_Factor_9123
selftext:
I see a lot of AI-generated games on here that look incredible, and I wanted to see if I could build something that was both fun to play and actually useful.

I've been building a language learning mobile app for about 10 months and felt like a game would be a nice addition.

The idea is pretty simple. You pick a language you're learning, set your skill level, and get dropped into a world where everyone speaks that language. The characters don't correct you or act like teachers. I wanted players to focus on accomplishing a task rather than worrying about making mistakes.

Here I'm checking in for a flight in Spanish. I'm actually speaking to the person behind the counter. Nothing is scripted, and the difficulty of the conversation changes based on how much Spanish I know.

Behind the scenes, AI keeps track of your conversations, picks up on mistakes you make, and gives you phrases to practice later. You can even sit down with an AI tutor and go over conversations you've had in the game.

You can walk around the airport, grab a coffee, go through security, take a taxi to a hotel, etc.

Basically, I wanted to recreate the experience of being dropped into a foreign country without having to buy a plane ticket.

I'm building this with Godot embedded inside native iOS and Android apps. One of the interesting development challenges has been getting AI-driven NPCs to behave like actual people doing their jobs rather than chatbots in a 3D world.

It's free on both platforms.

Curious what you guys think and whether anyone else has been experimenting with this kind of NPC interaction.
